text:
aya: Heads-up — we need to pick a prioritization approach for inference perf work (latency vs throughput vs cost) before next planning. short thread.

tom: Can we avoid a binary choice? I propose a slice-driven prioritization: identify customer slices and score options per-slice.

leah: +1. Use RICE but adapt for runtime constraints. Reach = monthly requests for slice, Impact = estimated SLO violations avoided (0-10), Confidence = % from telemetry, Effort = dev+infra weeks.

ben: Important: fold cost into the score somehow. $/token reductions matter for long-tail workloads. Suggest adding a cost_savings term.

aya: Example formula I sketched to keep things pragmatic:

```score = (reach * (impact + 0.5 * cost_savings) * confidence) / effort```

aya: Also add a binary flag for 'latency_hotpath' slices — give them a +20% multiplier to impact when low latency is customer-visible.

tom: Launch criteria proposal: p95 latency improvement >= 15% for hotpath slices, throughput (tokens/s) sustained at expected QPS, and infra cost delta per-10k tokens < $0.50. If any check fails, rollback.

leah: Sequencing idea: 1) quick wins (KV prefix cache + batching tweaks) that are low-risk and high-impact, 2) infra/quantization changes that reduce unit cost but require validation, 3) model/arch swaps with full eval & canary.

ben: Ops question — can Dedicated customers opt into canaries earlier? That would de-risk infra changes.

perf-bot: Deploy check created: PR-4567 linked, canary scheduled 2025-03-12 09:00 UTC :rocket: (will post metrics to #eng-runtime).

aya: I'll build a scoring sheet with per-slice numbers (reach, impact, confidence, effort, cost_savings) and rank top N. Quick sync tomorrow 10am PT?

tom: SGTM. I'll populate ACME / Scaleup / Internal dev slices with telemetry numbers before the sync.

leah: One more constraint — add a "regression budget" for quality: any perf change must not increase hallucination or drop eval score > 2 pts.

ben: ack. adding eval gating to the spreadsheet as a pass/fail column.

aya: Cool. If we can get the top 3 scored, we'll propose a two-sprint plan (hotpath sprint, then cost-savings sprint) at planning.

tom: Thanks — short and actionable.
